newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Banks freeze Yu Sung chequeing accounts.
newsitem.headline: Banks freeze Yu Sung chequeing accounts.

text.p: South Korean banks on Wednesday froze chequeing accounts of Yu Sung Co Ltd after the textile manufacturer defaulted on a further 110 million won of debt, a company executive said.
On Tuesday Yu Sung defaulted on 227 million won worth of promissary notes.
The executive said in a statement Yu Sung filed for court protection late on Tuesday after it failed to honour the notes. He gave no further details.
A company statement earlier said its financial trouble stemmed from difficulties in obtaining operating funds amid a depression in the textile industry.
The Korea Stock Exchange suspended trading in Yu Sung on Wednesday and said trading would resume from Friday, with shares placed on a supervision list.
Yu Sung's paid-in capital stood at 15 billion won and liabilities at 66.6 billion at the end of 1996.
